title: Accessible UI component
brief: Ask a coding agent for a React + TypeScript component that meets your team's bar: a typed props interface named <Component>Props, a named function export (export function <Component>), accessible labelling, and Tailwind classes instead of inline styles. No any types. Output only the component code.

lesson.summary: "Make a button" gets you a button. A team-ready component needs the constraints your reviewers enforce stated up front: types, export style, accessibility, and styling approach. Agents follow explicit standards well; they can't follow unwritten ones.
lesson.why_it_matters: Frontend agents produce plausible UI that quietly fails accessibility audits and design-system rules. Encoding your definition of done in the prompt (or a rules file) turns review comments into first-draft defaults.
lesson.strong_example:
Write a React + TypeScript component: {{component}}
Rules: props interface named <Name>Props; `export function <Name>`; accessible name via aria-label or <label>; Tailwind className only, no inline styles; no `any`. Output only the code.

vars.component: IconButton: a button that renders only an icon (passed in as a ReactNode prop) and calls onClick when pressed.

checks.label: No inline styles or any types

vars.component: SearchInput: a text input with a visible label, a placeholder, and an onChange callback that receives the string value.

checks.label: No inline styles or any types

vars.component: Toggle: an on/off switch with a text label that calls onChange(checked: boolean) when flipped.

checks.label: No inline styles or any types
Exposes its on/off state to assistive tech

rubric: The component is idiomatic React and would work as described
hints: Compare your prompt with the team's bar in the brief. Which of those rules would the agent have to guess?

This is about constraining code generation. List every non-negotiable as an explicit rule: naming, export style, typing, accessibility, and styling. Generic instructions like 'make it good' don't work.
Add a 'Rules:' list: props interface named <Name>Props; `export function <Name>`; aria-label or <label>; Tailwind className only, never style={{}}; never use any. Output only code.
reference_prompt:
You are a senior frontend engineer on a team with strict component standards.

Write a React + TypeScript component: {{component}}

Rules (all mandatory):
- Declare the props as `interface <ComponentName>Props`.
- Export it as a named function: `export function <ComponentName>(...)`.
- It must be accessible: interactive elements need an accessible name (aria-label or an associated <label>), and stateful controls expose their state (for example role="switch" with aria-checked).
- Style only with Tailwind classes in className. Never use inline style={{...}}.
- Never use the `any` type.

Output only the component code, with no explanation.
